decisions.reason: Report explicitly distinguishes the clipboard-text projection (InputState.draft, Occurrence.offset/length, chip expands to clipboardText) from the detect-text projection used by insertReference/consumeToken (chip = one U+FFFC), citing host-input-contract.ts JSDoc and the facade's detectText slicing/splicing, and notes plain text contributes equal width to both.

Locates snapshot.draft.length in add and explains paste #1 succeeds because both projections coincide on an empty composer, while paste #2 submits 29 against a 2-char detectText so the span splice fails and insertReference returns false, which the plugin converts to the changed-composer toast; explicitly rules out a real concurrent edit since the rev CAS passes.

Traces remove passing unconverted occurrence.offset/length (0..28) to consumeToken, the false return being ignored, records.delete running anyway, leaving the live occurrence and composer chip while the missing record triggers the dock's 'unavailable' sentinel — both symptoms tied to the same cross-projection mismatch plus ignored return value, not a separate upload failure.

Derives toDetectPos subtracting Σ(length−1) for occurrences before the position, applies it at both call sites: caret conversion accounting for all preceding occurrences on insert, and mapped offset with a one-character detect span (start, start+1) on removal; keeps the fresh-snapshot/draftRev guard and retires records only after consumeToken returns true (with distinct error state on false).

Proposes two successive pastes asserting both chips/occurrences exist, then removing a chip with another preceding chip (remove A, B survives with updated offsets), asserting composer occurrence, dock chip, and record are removed together; adds guard-refusal, first/last-chip, empty-again, and phase-guard variants with concrete assertions.
